html:
A council of the Catholic Church, held at Ferrara and then Florence from 1438, where the Greek and Latin churches agreed to end the split of the Great Schism.

Emperor John VIII, the patriarch of Constantinople and hundreds of Greek clergy and scholars came, because the Byzantines needed Western help against the Ottomans. Pope Eugene IV wanted the union to raise his standing over rival church councils. The two sides argued for months over the creed, purgatory, the bread used at communion and the power of the pope.

On 6 July 1439 the union was proclaimed. Only one Greek bishop, Mark of Ephesus, refused to sign. At home most Orthodox clergy and people rejected it, and the Russian church deposed the metropolitan who had signed. The promised help ended at the Battle of Varna.

The council had a second effect. Greek scholars such as Plethon and Bessarion met Italian humanists, which fed the revival of Plato in Florence.
sum: A council of the Catholic Church, held at Ferrara and then Florence from 1438, where the Greek and Latin churches agreed to end the split of the Great Schism.
